### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY (symbol, a top-level const object))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9a65a48f805dac70b64dc78c54abbe30dc0453d8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ebcc37c7e1e59361fa205e16276aedd36d129dcf` — the merge of head `d2c2cb98cb39e1a11c1caa1daea6aec61fb8ad1d` into base `9a65a48f805dac70b64dc78c54abbe30dc0453d8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ebcc37c7e1e59361fa205e16276aedd36d129dcf && git checkout ebcc37c7e1e59361fa205e16276aedd36d129dcf
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9a65a48f805dac70b64dc78c54abbe30dc0453d8 d2c2cb98cb39e1a11c1caa1daea6aec61fb8ad1d && git checkout -B drift-repro 9a65a48f805dac70b64dc78c54abbe30dc0453d8 && git merge --no-ff d2c2cb98cb39e1a11c1caa1daea6aec61fb8ad1d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9a65a48f805dac70b64dc78c54abbe30dc0453d8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9a65a48f805dac70b64dc78c54abbe30dc0453d8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c2e09545974c9dfc737e2f477258ebeea777bd8c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts, docs/adr/0084-application-builder-information-architecture.md + ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/studioMenuPlacement.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/studioMenuPlacement.test.ts
Security-touching: no

Read: card #37564 and its three comments (claim 7193675575, triage, dev report 7196303644), PR #37599's body and file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base `41164656`, 9 files, +192 / −34), and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built or run. The rest of the diff (`metadata-plugin.test.ts`, `StudioMenu.test.tsx`, `studioMenuModel.test.ts`, `StudioPaletteGroups.surfaceScope-36900.test.tsx`, the changeset's prose) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

On `Security-touching: no`: the hunks that name `position` change its menu tier and nothing else. No hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour; no access check, role or grant is read or written anywhere in the diff.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set — unchanged. Right.** `MetadataTypeRegistryEntrySchema.domain` keeps its six enum values (`metadata-plugin.zod.ts:391`). No author writes the registry. A `*.dataset.ts` item is validated by `ui/dataset.zod.ts#DatasetSchema`, which the diff does not touch; `filePatterns`, `loadOrder` (55), the overlay and create flags of the row are byte-identical.
- **Public surface — unchanged. Right.** No export, key or type is added or removed. `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` keeps its declared type; one element's `domain` value moves from `'ui'` to `'data'`.
- **Served value — changes, and is declared.** `GET /meta/types` answers `domain: "data"` for `dataset`, and the listing's domain-then-type sort (`protocol-discovery-and-bases.ts:766-768`) puts it first among the data types. `getTypeInfo` (`metadata-manager.ts:4073`) passes the same value. The PR body and the changeset both say so. Right.
- **No behaviour is keyed on the domain.** Read across `packages/` and `ui/`: the only readers of a registry entry's `domain` are that listing's sort, `getTypeInfo`, Studio's menu model (`studioMenuModel.ts:189`), the type directory (`DirectoryPage.tsx`) and the type page badge (`PageShell.tsx`). No write gate, loader, lint rule or serializer branches on it. `typescript-serializer.ts:64` (`['Dataset', 'ui']`) is the import subpath of the schema, not the domain, and is rightly left alone. The Console registers no local `dataset` resource, so `resolveResourceConfig` (`registry.ts:558`) falls through to the served value and cannot hold the old group.
- **Generated output — none owed.** `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Spec property liveness` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are success on the head.
- **Gate verdicts.** Every check-run on the head that ran concluded success (Test Core 1–10, Test UI 1–16, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, the lint and type-check lanes, Check Documentation Links). The skipped ones are opt-in or queue-only lanes.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` patch and `@object-ui/app-shell` patch, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset. Right on each count.

- **Clause-②: no** — the move is neither a widening nor a narrowing. For a published `@objectstack/spec` consumer, for Studio and for the docs, the set of values the `domain` field can hold, and the set of things the package accepts or exports, are what they were. One datum inside an exported constant differs. A `(narrowing)` arm would be wrong (nothing is refused or removed) and `yes` would be wrong (nothing is added).
- **Metadata-protocol: none** — nothing a metadata author can write changes meaning, default or acceptance, so neither `semantic` nor `added` applies.
- **Level** — `none` takes `patch` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist 3). The changeset body states the one consumer-visible effect in plain words: code that selected datasets by `domain === 'ui'` reads `'data'`. That is the honest release note for a value change and needs no BREAKING banner, since no declared capability is taken away.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` is empty. The dev's five `out_of_scope_findings`, each answered:

1. Claim written by the area, not the thread — process, no effect on the diff. Accepted.
2. `StudioPaletteGroups.surfaceScope-36900.test.tsx` outside the named surface — test only, two expectations that follow from `position` being always listed; the area confirmed it before the push. It is in the lane seat's remainder. Accepted.
3. Three pushes — no effect on this record, which names one head.
4. `dataset`'s schema stays in `packages/spec/src/ui/dataset.zod.ts` while the registry says `data`, and `adding-a-metadata-type.mdx` tells an author to place a schema under the matching domain folder. Agreed that it is not this card's: the amendment itself cites the schema at that path, the card asks for the registry value alone, and moving the file moves a published subpath export. The new registry comment says where the schema lives. Escalated to the seat as a follow-up question, not a finding on this head.
5. Read-only badge beside an enabled New button on the position page — not caused by this diff; the seat's to file.

SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. One consequence is noted, not a finding: `position` and `dataset` are now always-listed types, so a package's menu and palette read their lists even when the package holds none (the palette test's read set gains `position`). That is what the 常用 tier means and is ruled.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts`** — against the amendment on `main` (`#amendment-2026-11-26-moves`, first bullet) and its first consumer.

- The amendment: "its registered `domain` changes from `ui` to `data` in `…#DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY`… No special case is written into the menu for it." The diff does exactly that and nothing else on the row. `dashboard` and `report` stay `ui`, as the amendment says; no seventh domain value appears.
- The new comment, sentence by sentence: "a dataset is a `data` type — the semantic layer that charts and an AI's data questions both read" is the amendment's wording; "Studio lists it under 数据 Data, directly after `object`" holds through `studioMenuPlacement.ts` (index of `dataset` is index of `object` + 1) and `studioMenuModel.ts:189` (group is the served domain); "the row stays in this block because the overlay notes above name it" holds (the UI-block note names `dataset` twice for `allowEnvironmentOverlay`); "its schema still lives in `ui/dataset.zod.ts`" holds.
- Break attempts. Load order: unchanged at 55, below `report` and `dashboard` at 60. A stale local override in the Console: none exists for `dataset`. A consumer that filters by domain to decide behaviour: none found. The seed row's older comment ("last in the data domain") was already untrue before this change (`mapping` is 96) and is outside the diff.

**`docs/adr/0084-application-builder-information-architecture.md`** — against the registry and the placement list at this head, and the amendment it carries out.

- Table rows against the code, row by row: 数据 Data reads `object` 1 常用, `dataset` 2 常用, `picklist` 3, `hook` 4, `mapping` 5, `object_extension` 6, `seed` 7, `field` with no order; the registry holds exactly those eight under `data`, and the placement list holds them in that order and those tiers. 界面 UI reads `app`, `page`, `dashboard`, `report`, `view`, `action`, six rows, matching both. 访问 Access reads `permission` 1 常用, `position` 2 常用, then the four 高级 rows, matching both. They equal the three lists the amendment says the groups read "when the registry and the placement list have changed" (less `form`, not yet registered).
- The note under the table: 33 entries is right (32 one-line rows and `datasource`); the counts 8 · 6 · 2 · 7 · 6 · 4 sum to 33 and match the registry by domain; "where it was seventh… where it is second" is right; "`position` keeps its place" is right (Order 2 before and after).
- Form and authority. The edit is dated ("Rewritten 2026-11-26") and appended the way the record appends: the 2026-11-25 note under the table is left whole, a new italic note follows it, and the "not redrawn today" paragraph is marked where it stands instead of being reworded. It uses the amendment's own verb ("a row is rewritten, or written, in the change that moves it… the same pull request… needs no further ruling"), and it says it "decides nothing". Everything it states as placed is ruled: `dataset` in 数据 Data directly after `object` by the maintainer's 「数据集 是AI 也要用的吧？不能算界面吧」 and epic #37424's decision 6; both types in 常用 by name by ruling record 7187264388 on #37451 (question 4, yes). No Status-line entry is owed, since no decision is added. It does not touch `datasource` or `form`, and adds no second table of the pinned shape.
- N8: fixed as contract record 7189689403 on PR #37518 asked. "the note below" now reads as a link to `#amendment-2026-11-26-position`, and that anchor exists (the 2026-11-26 section "What Studio is").

**`studioMenuPlacement.ts`** (implementing) — agrees with the contract. `dataset` directly after `object`, `position` directly after `permission`, both `common`, both removed from the advanced block; twelve common and twenty advanced rows. Each row's comment gives the amendment's own reason: test 1 for `dataset` (`DatasetSchema.object` is required, `dataset.zod.ts:892`), test 3 for `position` (ADR-0150 D7). The header's "Placements by name" paragraph restates the 2026-11-25 rule without rewording it. No group is stored: the file still holds order and tier only.

**`studioMenuPlacement.test.ts`** (the enforcing gate) — the three-way pin (registry, list, ADR rows) is unchanged in logic and passes on the rewritten rows; the literal lists are updated; the new cases pin adjacency and the three touched groups. `Test UI` is success on the head.

Nits, neither with an effect on correctness or the contract:

- N1 (nit) — the mark added to the "not redrawn today" paragraph, "(Since rewritten: …)", carries no date of its own, where every other mark in the record opens "Amended YYYY-MM-DD:". It links the dated note under the table, so a reader cannot be misled. Date it when the branch merges `main`, or leave it.
- N2 (nit) — three sibling marks of the 2026-11-26 amendment still read in the future tense for `dataset` ("is to be registered `data`": TL;DR 4, the stands table's TL;DR 4 row, and the two-tiers note). They are dated statements and true as written on their day; only the one paragraph got a "since" mark. Leave as an accepted deviation.

**Seat questions**

1. Yes. The spec change agrees with the rewritten rows sentence by sentence and with `studioMenuPlacement.ts`; the detail is above. The pin test that compares all three is green on the head.
2. Neither a widening nor a narrowing. A reader of a type's domain sees a different value for one type and the same set of possible values. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch` on both packages are right, and the changeset names the one effect on code that filtered by `domain === 'ui'`.
3. Yes, as asked: the mark links `#amendment-2026-11-26-position`.
4. Yes. Dated, appended as a note and a mark with the earlier text left standing, and it presents as placed only what the maintainer ruled (ruling record 7187264388 on #37451 for the tiers; the maintainer's words and decision 6 of epic #37424 for the group and the place). One mark is undated (N1).
5. None. No other type changes group or tier, and no relative order changes. What a reader sees move as a consequence: the Order numbers of `picklist` to `seed` are each one higher; the 界面 UI fold ends at `action`; the 访问 Access fold starts at `assignment_rule`; the type directory and the `/meta/types` listing count one more data type and one fewer UI type; the palette, which draws the menu's entries, always lists `dataset` and `position` on a package and reads their lists.
